steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In January 1923, French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr, Germany's industrial heartland, after Germany defaulted on reparations payments. The German government responded with a policy of passive resistance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: By November 1923, the German mark had become virtually worthless. At the peak of hyperinflation, 4.2 trillion marks equalled $1 USD. A loaf of bread that cost 1 mark in 1919 cost 200,000 million marks by November 1923. Workers were paid twice daily and given time off to spend their wages before they lost further value.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The mark had been losing value since the war - Germany had funded WWI by printing money rather than raising taxes, doubling the money supply between 1914-1918. The Ruhr crisis accelerated an existing problem into a catastrophe.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hyperinflation destroyed the confidence of the German middle class in the Weimar Republic. Many who had been reasonably prosperous were reduced to poverty, and they blamed the democratic government for their suffering. This anger would later fuel support for extremist parties like the Nazis.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why France occupied the Ruhr in January 1923. (4 marks) | How far did hyperinflation affect all groups in German society equally? (8 marks) | "Hyperinflation was the worst crisis the Weimar Republic faced in the years 1919-1923." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: France occupied the Ruhr because Germany defaulted on reparations payments - specifically failing to deliver timber (December 1922) and coal (January 1923). French Prime Minister Poincaré was determin | Hyperinflation did NOT affect all groups equally. Borrowers benefited because they could repay debts with worthless money. Industrialists who sold goods for foreign currency profited. Farmers benefite | Hyperinflation was an extremely serious crisis because it destroyed the savings of the middle class, caused widespread starvation, and shattered confidence in the Republic. It also triggered the Munic

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use specific figures: 4.2 trillion marks = $1; 60,000 French troops; 132 workers killed For impact questions, structure your answer by GROUP (winners/losers or class by class) The key chain of causation is: Default → Ruhr occupation → Passive resistance → Print money → Hyperinflation Remember that hyperinflation had begun BEFORE 1923 - WWI spending and reparations had already weakened the mark The Rentenmark was backed by LAND and INDUSTRY, not gold - this is a common exam question When evaluating Stresemann, note that the recovery was built on American loans, which were fragile Link hyperinflation to political consequences: it pushed the middle class towards extremism and destroyed trust in democracy
